name: Vivi Ornitier
oracle_text:
{0}: Add X mana in any combination of {U} and/or {R}, where X is Vivi Ornitier's power. Activate only during your turn and only once each turn.
Whenever you cast a noncreature spell, put a +1/+1 counter on Vivi Ornitier and it deals 1 damage to each opponent.
blocked_sentences: {0}: Add X mana in any combination of {U} and/or {R}, where X is Vivi Ornitier's power. Activate only during your turn and only once each turn.

needs.what: add_mana needs to produce N mana divided freely among a fixed printed set of colors, with the division chosen by the controller as the mana ability resolves -- e.g. `{"op": "add_mana", "mana": ["U", "R"], "amount": {"power_of": {"self_only": true}}, "any_combination": true}`, where a power of 4 may be taken as UURR, UUUR, RRRR, and so on. That is one decision of N independent per-pip color choices (or an equivalent 'how many of each' split), asked at resolution and legal inside a mana ability.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: add_mana's own keys are amount, mana, player, reflecting and in_commander_identity. `amount` scales a single mana type, so `mana: "U"` with amount X is X blue and nothing else. The only branching a mana ability is allowed is the documented `choose_mode` whose modes each contain only add_mana, and that offers a single up-front pick -- 'X of {U}' OR 'X of {R}' -- never a mix, so a power-4 Vivi could not make UURR. Nesting `repeat`, `for_each` or `may` around the add_mana to choose one pip at a time is forbidden by the same rule (a mana ability may contain only add_mana, or one choose_mode of add_manas). `in_commander_identity` is the one key that does yield a free combination, but it reads the controller's commander's color identity rather than the card's own printed {U}/{R}: it is right only in a deck where Vivi is the commander and wrong everywhere else (Vivi in the 99 of a five-color deck would tap for any five colors), which is a silent divergence rather than the printed ability. `add_mana_per` multiplies one mana type by a count and has no amount/split of its own.
